description: After build:shared the module resolves from packages/tickets, packages/co-managed, server and shared/workflow, and imports no server action
Matrix returns the expected level for all 25 Impact x Urgency pairs and rejects values outside 1 to 5
Each diagonal pair (n, n) maps to level n
listPrioritiesForBoard on an ITIL board returns exactly the five ITIL ticket priorities in level order
listPrioritiesForBoard on a non-ITIL board returns only the tenant's own ticket priorities and no project-task priorities
listPrioritiesForBoard treats a NULL priority_type as the tenant's own kind
listPrioritiesForBoard never returns another tenant's priorities
findBoardFieldProblems reports an own priority on an ITIL board and an ITIL priority on a non-ITIL board, naming both
findBoardFieldProblems reports a priority id that does not exist or is a project-task priority
The existing priorityBoardType integration tests pass unchanged against the delegating helpers
A patch without priority_id or board_id on a ticket with a non-fitting priority reports no priority problem
A patch that changes only board_id is checked against the ticket's stored priority
A patch that changes only the title on a ticket with a category from another board reports no category problem
resolveItilPriorityId finds the ITIL priority after it has been renamed
resolveItilPriorityId returns null when the tenant has no ITIL priority for the level
defaultPriorityForBoard returns the stored default when it fits the board
defaultPriorityForBoard ignores a stored default of the wrong family and returns level 3 on an ITIL board
defaultPriorityForBoard returns the lowest-order own ticket priority on a non-ITIL board with no default, and null when the tenant has none
ITIL board, Impact and Urgency supplied: priority is the matrix result and a supplied priority_id is ignored
ITIL board, priority only, no stored Impact/Urgency: priority accepted and both stay empty
ITIL board, priority only, refuse policy, own-family priority: refused with a priority_id problem
Fallback returns the configured priority when it fits
Fallback returns the board default when the configured priority does not fit
Fallback returns the configured priority unchanged when the tenant has no priority of the board's family
Fallback with only one of Impact and Urgency drops both
Non-ITIL board with Impact and Urgency supplied: both come back empty and the supplied priority is used
Seeding ITIL priorities twice leaves five rows
Seeding with a tenant priority already named like an ITIL one fails with an error naming it and does not flag it
Inbound defaults form on an ITIL board offers only ITIL priorities; on a non-ITIL board only the tenant's own
Changing the board to one of the other kind clears the selected priority; changing between boards of the same kind keeps it
Saving inbound defaults with a wrong-family priority fails with a priority field error and stores nothing
Saving inbound defaults with a deleted priority fails with a priority field error
Saving an existing non-fitting row with only its description changed and the priority untouched is refused with the same error
A stored row with a non-fitting priority renders the warning in the form and the badge in the list; a fitting row renders neither
Email to a board whose default row has a fitting priority creates the ticket with that priority
Email to a board whose default row has a non-fitting priority creates the ticket with the board's default priority
Email to a board with a non-fitting priority and no fitting priority in the tenant still creates the ticket, with the configured priority
Email to a board whose default row points at a deleted priority creates the ticket with the board's default priority
Every new inbound-defaults key exists in every locale and passes the glossary checks
Fixture produces two ITIL boards, one non-ITIL board and one mixed board with the expected kinds, priorities and categories
The suite fails when a surface listed in the PRD has no row in the table
After migration, categories has standard_category_id and the partial unique index
A flagged category with a standard name and parent gets the matching standard_category_id
A flagged category with a non-standard name loses the flag and gets no link
A flagged category on a non-ITIL board loses the flag and stays on that board
A tenant with one set and three ITIL boards ends with three complete sets, one per board, each child under its own board's parent
An ITIL board with a partial set gets only the missing rows
A tenant with ITIL boards and no flagged categories at all gets a full set per board
A ticket on the second ITIL board using a shared category ends up on that board's copy with the same name and parent
A ticket on the board that held the set keeps its category id
A ticket on a non-ITIL board using a formerly flagged category keeps its category id
Templates, recurring definitions, their overrides and inbound defaults on the second ITIL board point at that board's copy
A workflow action input naming the second ITIL board and a shared category is re-pointed; one naming no board is unchanged
Inserting a second row for the same board and standard category violates the index
Running the migration twice produces the same rows
The migration runs against a Citus-distributed schema
Ticket priority_id, itil_impact and itil_urgency are identical before and after the migration for every ticket
A freshly seeded dev database has the ITIL set on the ITIL board and none on other boards
listCategoriesForBoard returns the same 35 names for two ITIL boards, with different ids
listCategoriesForBoard on a non-ITIL board returns only its own categories
listCategoriesForBoard on an ITIL board also returns a non-standard category attached to it
getTicketCategoriesByBoard, ticket-form hydration and GET /api/v1/tickets/categories return the same list for the same board
A category from another board is reported, on ITIL and non-ITIL boards
A subcategory whose parent is not the ticket's category is reported
A template and a recurring schedule on the second ITIL board save with a standard category and generate an occurrence
Co-managed edit and the maintenance-ticket workflow action accept a standard category on the second ITIL board
Creating a second ITIL board gives it 35 rows and changes no row on any other board
A non-ITIL board's category named like a standard one keeps its flag, board and children when an ITIL board is created
Two ITIL boards created concurrently end with one set each
Deleting one of two ITIL boards leaves the other board's set intact
The itilBoardDeletionCleanup integration tests are updated and pass
Web update, re-parent and delete of a standard row on an ITIL board are refused
REST update and delete and reference-data delete of a standard row on an ITIL board are refused
Web add and REST create of a category on an ITIL board are refused; on a non-ITIL board they succeed
Copy to an ITIL board is refused; copy from an ITIL board to a non-ITIL board creates plain categories
updateTicketCategory ignores or rejects board_id, is_from_itil_standard and standard_category_id in its input
Each category mutation is refused for a user without the ticket_settings permission
REST delete of a category used only as a ticket's subcategory is refused
Categories settings on the second ITIL board shows 35 rows with the Standard badge and no enabled edit, delete or add
The copy dialog lists no ITIL board as a target
CSV import to the second ITIL board matches a standard category by name
CSV import to an ITIL board with an unknown category reports the row and creates no category
Surface suite: each listed category picker returns the 35 standard categories for the second ITIL board
Every new category key exists in every locale and passes the glossary checks
MSP create on an ITIL board with Impact and Urgency stores the matrix priority and both values
MSP create on a non-ITIL board with Impact and Urgency in the form stores neither and uses the selected priority
MSP update of Impact alone on an assessed ITIL ticket recomputes the priority from the new Impact and stored Urgency
No source file matches the P-number name pattern lookup
Direct change to the level-2 priority on an assessed ticket stores Impact 2 and Urgency 2
Direct priority change on an unassessed ticket leaves Impact and Urgency empty
MSP create with Impact and no Urgency on an ITIL board is refused with a field error
A service request configured with Impact and Urgency creates a ticket with the matrix priority found by level
A template with Impact and Urgency instantiates with the matrix priority even when its stored priority differs
Batch duplicate copies priority, Impact and Urgency so they agree
A create or update that sends itil_priority_level does not store it
Ticket event payloads carry the level of the ticket's priority for an ITIL ticket and none for other tickets
Ticket detail for an ITIL ticket without Impact and Urgency shows its stored priority and Not assessed
Choosing Impact and Urgency on that ticket shows and saves the matrix priority
Every new Impact/Urgency key exists in every locale and passes the glossary checks
createTicket with policy refuse rejects a wrong-family priority and a category from another board
createTicket with policy fallback creates the ticket with the board default priority and without the foreign category
The ticketCreateFieldPersistence and ticketCreateBoardStatusValidation integration tests pass
Client portal create with a wrong-family priority id is refused
CSV import with rows for an ITIL and a non-ITIL board imports the fitting rows and reports the others
CSV import row without a priority gets its board's default priority
Teams message action on a board whose stored default is of the wrong family creates the ticket with a fitting priority
Maintenance-ticket action with a wrong-family priority fails the action with a field error
RMM alert with a mapped priority of the wrong family creates the ticket with the board default
RMM priority lookup never returns a project-task priority
Huntress incident with a severity mapped to a wrong-family priority creates the ticket with the board default
Telephony auto-ticket and renewal ticket with a non-fitting configured priority are created with the board default
Workflow tickets.create with a wrong-family priority creates the ticket with the board default
Inbound webhook create with a category from another board creates the ticket without a category
Service request without a configured priority uses the board default and never a project-task priority
Data-migration import of a ticket with a non-fitting priority imports it with the board default
REST create with a category from another board returns 400 with a category_id error
Surface suite: every create writer on the second ITIL board stores a fitting priority and a category owned by that board
prepareTicketFieldPatch returns the patch unchanged when it touches none of board, priority, Impact, Urgency, category or subcategory
Both MSP update functions refuse a category from another board
REST update with a subcategory that is not a child of the category returns 400
REST update with a priority only on an assessed ITIL ticket stores the diagonal Impact and Urgency
Workflow tickets.update_fields with a wrong-family priority fails with a field error
Inbound webhook update that changes the board without a fitting priority is refused
Activities inline priority update with a wrong-family priority is refused, for both action variants
Bundle sync leaves the priority of a child on a board of the other family and updates a child on a board of the same family
Moving a ticket from an ITIL to a non-ITIL board without a priority is refused; with a fitting priority it saves and clears Impact and Urgency
Bulk move across families reports each refused ticket and moves none of them
Moving a ticket between two ITIL boards keeps the same category and subcategory by name, with the destination board's ids
Moving a ticket between two non-ITIL boards without a category in the patch clears category and subcategory
A ticket with a wrong-family priority saves a title, status, assignee and description change through MSP, REST and workflow update
A ticket with a category from another board saves the same changes
The helper returns ITIL priorities for an ITIL board, own priorities otherwise, and treats a missing kind as own
The existing QuickAddTicket.boardScopedPriorities tests pass
Workflow designer priority picker with an ITIL board selected lists only ITIL priorities, in both copies
Huntress severity mapping lists only priorities that fit the selected board
Co-managed edit options for an ITIL ticket contain only ITIL priorities and a patch with another is rejected
Service request editor on a non-ITIL board lists no ITIL priority
Create ticket from asset lists only priorities the server accepts for the selected board
Activities inline picker for a ticket on an ITIL board lists only ITIL priorities
CSV import dialog offers ITIL priorities for rows of an ITIL board when the default board is not ITIL
Inbound webhook and RMM alert rule priority lookups return no project-task priority
GET /api/v1/tickets/priorities with board_id returns only fitting priorities, with itil_priority_level; without it, behaviour is unchanged
Mobile ticket detail for a ticket with no priority on an ITIL board lists only ITIL priorities
Surface suite: every priority picker lists the same priorities for both ITIL boards and none the server refuses
The existing board action tests (mutation guard, portal status guard, co-managed deactivation) pass against the extracted functions
POST /api/v1/boards for an ITIL board produces the same statuses, categories, default priority and SLA assignment as the web action
POST /api/v1/boards for a non-ITIL board has seeded statuses
The first ITIL board in a tenant that has own priorities gets an ITIL default priority
The first ITIL board in a tenant with no priorities at all gets the level-3 ITIL default
Create and update with a default priority of the wrong family are refused
Create with ITIL categories and own priorities, and the reverse, is refused on web and REST
Renaming an existing mixed board saves; changing one of its kinds to another mixed combination is refused
A board created with a default team has it stored
The create result and BOARD_CREATED payload carry the assigned sla_policy_id
A board created by reference-data import or onboarding has a default priority and, when ITIL, its categories
DELETE /api/v1/boards on the default board, a board with tickets and a board used by inbound defaults is refused with the web's reason
DELETE /api/v1/boards on an unused board removes its statuses and categories
switchBoardType is refused without the ticket_settings permission
Switching a non-ITIL board to ITIL gives it 35 standard categories, keeps its own categories and sets an ITIL default priority
Switching to ITIL in a tenant with no ITIL priorities creates the five
Switching an ITIL board to the tenant's own kind leaves its categories editable and sets an own default priority
Switching the only ITIL board to the tenant's own kind deletes no priority and no category
After a switch in either direction, every ticket, inbound default, template and schedule on the board is unchanged
After a switch to ITIL, the board's sla_policy_id is unchanged
The summary counts match the open tickets, inbound defaults, templates and schedules whose priority will not fit
Switching to the tenant's own kind in a tenant with only ITIL ticket priorities is refused with the message
The confirmation shows the summary and switches only on confirm; cancel changes nothing
A legacy mixed board shows both kinds read-only and offers the switch
PUT /api/v1/boards with a changed kind runs the switch; with an unchanged kind it does not touch categories or priorities
Every new board-type key exists in every locale and passes the glossary checks
After initializeApp, creating an ITIL board through the server action without rendering any MSP page assigns the ITIL policy
The same holds in a production build, for the server action and for POST /api/v1/boards
ITIL setup with no hook registered throws on a PSA tenant and is skipped without error on an AlgaDesk tenant
The migration flags the policy named ITIL Standard and no other; a second flagged policy in a tenant is rejected
After the ITIL policy is renamed, creating another ITIL board reuses it and creates no second policy
A tenant's own unflagged policy named ITIL Standard is not adopted or deleted
Creating an ITIL board when the policy has no targets for the current ITIL priorities adds five; edited targets keep their values
itilSlaService and ensureSlaParity create identical targets and thresholds
Updating a board, switching its kind and running this plan's migrations leave sla_policy_id unchanged on every board
A new ITIL board created with an explicit SLA policy keeps that policy
A ticket with an SLA emits stage-entered with the ticket's resolution due time as the target

No source file imports a removed itilUtils export
ticketFieldOptionsActions has no unused exports and no console.log
The repository builds and the email and category tests pass with both removed
Board create and update on web and REST succeed with the columns dropped, and a request that still sends them is accepted and ignored
The guard passes on the repository after this plan
The guard fails on a fixture file that queries categories by board_id outside the allow-list, and on one that updates tickets.priority_id directly
The contract test fails when a listed writer stops importing the shared rules
Every table, column, function and file named in the doc exists in the repository
docs/itil holds only itil-integration.md and no doc links to the old plan path
The report runs read-only against a migrated database and returns no category rows for a tenant with two clean ITIL boards
The generated OpenAPI matches the route schemas with no diff after regeneration
